scenes.name: The Choice
scenes.display: The princess Sāvitrī shone so brightly that no prince dared ask for her hand. So she went forth to choose for herself — and in a forest hermitage she chose Satyavān, son of a blind and exiled king.
scenes.tts: The princess Sah-vit-ree shone so brightly, that no prince dared ask for her hand. So she went forth to choose for herself; and in a forest hermitage, she chose Sut-yuh-vaan, son of a blind and exiled king.

scenes.name: Nārada's Word
scenes.display: But the sage Nārada brought her father news no father wants to hear: the boy was flawless in every virtue that mattered — and in one year, he would die. Sāvitrī answered only, "The heart is given once. I have given mine."
scenes.tts: But the sage Naa-rud-ah brought her father news no father wants to hear: the boy was flawless in every virtue that mattered; and in one year, he would die. Sah-vit-ree answered only, the heart is given once. I have given mine.

scenes.name: Counting the Days
scenes.display: She folded away her silks, put on rough bark-cloth, and took up the hermitage's small daily work — telling no one, only counting the days. For the last three nights she stood fasting, still as a lamp in windless air.
scenes.tts: She folded away her silks, put on rough bark cloth, and took up the hermitage's small daily work; telling no one, only counting the days. For the last three nights she stood fasting, still as a lamp in windless air.

scenes.name: The Fated Day
scenes.display: On the appointed morning she followed him into the forest. At noon, the axe slipped from Satyavān's hand. "My head," he said, "is splitting." And he laid it in her lap, and was still.
scenes.tts: On the appointed morning she followed him into the forest. At noon, the axe slipped from Sut-yuh-vaan's hand. My head, he said, is splitting. And he laid it in her lap, and was still.

scenes.name: The Dark King
scenes.display: Then Sāvitrī saw him: a figure dark as a rain-cloud, robed in red, a noose coiled in his hand. It was Yama, King of the Dead, come in person for so virtuous a soul. He drew out a spark no bigger than a thumb, and turned south. And she followed.
scenes.tts: Then Sah-vit-ree saw him: a figure dark as a rain cloud, robed in red, a noose coiled in his hand. It was Yum-ah, King of the Dead, come in person for so virtuous a soul. He drew out a spark no bigger than a thumb, and turned south. And she followed.

scenes.name: Walking with Death
scenes.display: "Walk with the wise but seven steps," she said, "and you are friends." Pleased, Yama offered her boon after boon — anything but the life he carried. Sight for the blind king. A kingdom restored. And then, quietly: "a hundred sons, born of me and Satyavān." The Lord of Death stopped walking.
scenes.tts: Walk with the wise but seven steps, she said, and you are friends. Pleased, Yum-ah offered her boon after boon; anything but the life he carried. Sight for the blind king. A kingdom restored. And then, quietly: a hundred sons, born of me and Sut-yuh-vaan. The Lord of Death stopped walking.

scenes.name: The Return
scenes.display: For her word could not come true unless his life was returned. Caught by his own boon, Yama smiled, and loosed the noose. Satyavān woke as if from sleep, and his father opened his eyes on a world made new. Sāvitrī walked her husband home at dusk, having out-argued Death itself.
scenes.tts: For her word could not come true unless his life was returned. Caught by his own boon, Yum-ah smiled, and loosed the noose. Sut-yuh-vaan woke as if from sleep, and his father opened his eyes on a world made new. Sah-vit-ree walked her husband home at dusk, having out-argued Death itself.
